card.intuition: A skill is a teachable capability bundled as a unit of instructions and resources kept in the environment until a context pointer pulls it into the context window for the task at hand. Only the name and description sit in context by default; the full body loads when triggered.
card.analogy: A recipe card in a drawer: the index shows the one-line name, and you pull out the full card only when you actually cook that dish.
card.time_complexity: O(description-only per turn): only the name and description sit in context, saving tokens until the matching task loads the rest.
card.space_complexity: O(sentence or two by default): a skill takes up almost no room in the finite context window however large its full instructions are.
when_to_use: When placing a deploy runbook so the agent loads it only when the task involves deploys
When scaffolding a new service or writing a migration that should be read only when that kind of work comes up
When you want an open standard format (a SKILL.md plus optional scripts and templates) that works across major harnesses
gotchas: Distinguish a skill from a tool — a tool is what the agent calls; a skill is instructions it reads
Do not put a skill's full body in AGENTS.md, where it would burn tokens every turn for something used weekly
A skill only helps if its description is specific enough for the agent to trigger it at the right time

steps.label: Pack
steps.annotation: The skill folder holds a SKILL.md with a name and description, optionally scripts, templates, and reference material.

steps.label: Register
steps.annotation: Only the one-line name and description sit in context by default, taking near zero room.

steps.label: Trigger
steps.annotation: When the agent task matches the description, it pulls the full skill instructions into the context window.

steps.label: Run
steps.annotation: The agent runs the skill's scripts or follows its instructions for the task at hand.

exercise.prompt: Write a function that decides whether a skill should load based on its description matching a task. Return the body path when matched, else None.
hints: The skill body should stay out of context when the task does not match
A missing match should evaluate falsy, so None is the clean return
exercise.test_code:
assert should_load('deploy', 'preparing a deploy', 'skills/deploy/SKILL.md') == 'skills/deploy/SKILL.md'
assert should_load('deploy', 'writing a test', 'skills/deploy/SKILL.md') is None
print('PASS')
